primary_claim: A LoRA adapter trained via Diff Interpretation Tuning (DIT) enables a finetuned model to accurately report hidden behaviors encoded in its own weight diff (e.g. a hidden persona gated behind a secret trigger), substantially outperforming black-box baselines, and generalizes to held-out weight diffs, unseen triggers, and higher-rank or full-parameter finetunes it wasn't trained on.

effect.metric: 5-point-scale accuracy of reported hidden topic / news headline vs. ground truth
effect.value: DIT shows strong performance on held-out hidden-topic and news-headline weight diffs, much stronger than black-box baselines

stated_future_work: Develop techniques for certifying the correctness of WeightDiffQA answers
limitations_stated: DIT-adapters show poor cross-behavior generalization: hidden-topic adapters struggle to summarize news knowledge and vice versa
DIT fails to report the trigger phrases that gate hidden behaviors -- a DIT-adapter trained to predict a 3-digit SEP code trigger does no better than random guessing
DIT answers come with no certification of correctness by default, making them potentially unreliable since LLMs can hallucinate, confabulate, or be deceptive
quote: We then test the DIT-adapter on 100 held-out hidden-topic weight diffs and observe strong performance, much stronger than simple black-box methods are able to achieve.
